data.narrative:
Still Bright, a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Jon Vardner and Professors Alan C. West and Scott Banta, has raised $18.7M to date. The climate and energy sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the peer-median method does not apply here: while eight same-sector companies exist, insufficient datapoints meet narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier)—zero comps satisfied these thresholds—requiring a minimum of three to avoid misleading sector-wide averages.

Consequently, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised ($19M) as a value proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to the subsequent stage yields an implied valuation of $47M. This single-method triangulation establishes a range of $40M (low) to $54M (median $47M), anchored to standard progression mechanics rather than peer trading multiples.

Key uncertainties remain substantial: the absence of tightly comparable seed-stage peers limits confidence in the 2.5x multiplier's applicability to Still Bright's specific technology and market position. A more robust valuation would require either comparable company data from the climate-energy seed cohort or forward-looking revenue or technical milestone benchmarks. Current analysis supports a $40M–$54M range pending further dataset development.
